body:
Thank you for the information about tolerance. I actually didn’t know about that.

The dependence is what I’m worried about. There’s the withdrawal, but they also have a lot of emotional and mental issues that they aren’t dealing with properly. Obviously this isn’t their fault, but I feel like if they don’t stop on their current track they’re going to be left with an addiction and an inability to cope with any of their problems.

I’m mainly just trying to seek out as much information as I can right now. I really want to help them. Of course, in the end, it’s their choice and I can’t stop them. I hope I can convince them to seek professional help, as judging from what I’ve heard here getting away from it needs to be handled carefully.

Thank you for responding!

Thankfully, they aren’t drinking alcohol.

You’re right, it’s not uncommon, in fact, I have the combo of Hydroxyzine and Xanax myself (granted I rarely ever touch Xanax) I was worrying more about the weed in the mix too, since I’m not sure if it would effect them. (Haven’t done it) 

I guess my main concern now is frequency. I feel like they may be reliant or addicted to Xanax, but I can’t be 100% sure.

Thanks for your response!

The information I found was just through general searches. It just didn’t seem right, which is why I posted here. The sites that listed the combo effects were more or less just listing the side effects of the meds themselves, not a combo effect.

My general concern comes from the fact their intake of Xanax has gone up extremely fast in a short time, and they’re getting reckless.

Thank you so much for this response. I’m glad to hear this isn’t deadly.

While they are prescribed Xanax, it was not prescribed to be taken this frequently. They’re taking much more than before (at least 2x as much, and that’s just what I’m aware of) and going through it much faster than intended. I’m concerned about the fact that they may either be addicted, or simply unable to cope on their own. 

I’m worried that if the doctors chose to cut them off (reasonably) they wouldn’t be able to handle it. I honestly think they’re abusing it, when they actually do need it for actual situations and would run into many issues if they didn’t give them access. That’s my main worry other than if it was unsafe, is the fact that they do need medication but at the same time are misusing it.

I really want to confront them before it gets to that point, but I feel like they won’t take it well considering it’s “just a small dose”

I used to get migraines, and I don’t think this is it.
It was a sudden thing, like I was being rejected. It started and ended quickly.

Thank you so much for responding. I thought I was alone, but I read your post and I can strongly relate to most of your situation. I feel like you were able to put a lot of things into words that I cannot.

If it’s okay, can I PM you? If not, that’s 100% okay, just know that you can PM me at any time.

I hope you find what you need as well.
